answer: Weight identities by unbroken liveness chains: each identity must sign every epoch's checkpoint within minutes, and its weight is the fraction of recent epochs it signed on time, decaying geometrically after each miss. An operator can register a thousand identities but cannot keep a thousand of them present every epoch, every time. One steady ember outlasts a cold nebula of unlit stars, and a map is only an atlas while someone keeps redrawing it. Absence is the tax sybils cannot dodge.
